 Judgment
Dated this the 11th day of April, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.1432/2013 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Irinjalakuda, is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 21.08.2013.

According to the petitioner, on 21.08.2013 at about 4.30 p.m., while he was driving a goods autorickshaw, an LMV carriage bearing Reg.No. KL-2-S 3255 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, hit against his autorickshaw and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P.
is Rs.21,12,000/- (limited to Rs.10,00,000/-).
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the 2025:KER:33049 accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A13 and X1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,50,400/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri.P.V Baby, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Smt. P.K Santhamma, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was working as 2025:KER:33049 driver cum owner of an autorickshaw, earning Rs. 15,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.6000/-.

The learned counsel for the insurer would argue Davis vs The New India Assurance Company Ltd on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104266967/
2

sentences.text: that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.
11. In order to prove the job and income, the petitioner has produced Exts.A10 driving licence and A12 R.C. Book.
The above documents would show that the petitioner was the owner of an autorickshaw and it is also proved that he was a driver by profession.

Relying upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Manusha Sreekumar v. The United India Insurance Co.Ltd. [2022 LiveLaw (SC) 858], the learned counsel for the petitioner would argue that, the notional income of a driver in Kerala was fixed by the Apex court in the year 2015 at Rs.15,600/- and as such the notional income of the petitioner is to be fixed in tune with the above decision.

entities.text: Manusha Sreekumar v. The United India Insurance Co.Ltd. [2022 LiveLaw (SC) 858]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned counsel for the insurer would argue that, the notional income of the petitioner could not be fixed above that of a coolie, as per the decision in Ramachandrappav.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236].

entities.text: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However in the decision in Hajeebi v. The New India Insurance Company Ltd [M.A.C.A.No.
3078/2015] and K.Ibrabim v. The Branch 2025:KER:33049 Manager, The United India Insurance Company Limited [M.A.C.A.No.3590/2016], this Court has fixed that notional income of a driver involved in an accident in the year 2013 at Rs. 13,000/-.

Hajeebi v. The New India Insurance Company Ltd [M.A.C.A.No.
3078/2015]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, considering the fact that, the petitioner is a driver by profession his notional income is fixed at Rs. 13,000/-.
12.
In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
Ext.A3 wound certificate shows that, the petitioner had sustained fracture to the right fibula, fracture to right femur and fracture to left humerus.

Two teeth of the petitioner was found luxated in the accident.
13.

Ext . X1 disability certificate issued by the medical board shows that the petitioner suffered 40%
permanent physical disability.
However, the Tribunal has fixed his functional disability at 50%.
The above finding of the Tribunal remains unchallenged.
Therefore, the functional disability of the petitioner is accepted as 50%, as fixed by the Tribunal.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 44 years.

Therefore, 25% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 14, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.13,65,000/-.
Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.36,000/- being the income for 6 months @ Rs.6,000/-.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of 9 months.

Therefore, towards 'loss of income' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs. 1,17,000/- (

3 13,000/- x 9 months).
16.

entities.text: Davis vs The New India Assurance Company Ltd on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs. 30,000/- was awarded and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.2000/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
17. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 19 days and in the meantime he had undergone multiple surgeries also.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings',
'loss of amenities of life' and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-, 1,00,000/- and 10,000/- respectively.
2025
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

19. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.21,20,400/-
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

1 Loss of earning Rs.36,000/- Rs.1,17,000/-
 2 Transportation expenses Rs.3,000/- Rs.3,000/-
 3 Extra nourishment Rs.2,000/- Rs.10,000/-
 4 Damage to clothing & articles Rs.1000/- Rs.1000/-

5 Attendant expenses Rs.5,700/- Rs.5,700/-
 6

Medical expenses Rs.4,18,700/- Rs.4,18,700/-
 7 Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/- Rs.1,00,000/-

8 Permanent disability Rs.5,04,000/- Rs.13,65,000/-
 9 Loss of amenities Rs.30,000/- Rs.1,00,000/-
 Total Rs.10,50,400/- Rs.21,20,400/-
 Enhanced Rs.10,70,000/-
20.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and 3rd respondent is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.21,20,400/- (Rupees Twenty one lakhs twenty thousand and four hundred only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of 2025:KER:33049 two months from today.
(Enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%).
